shots.text: In nineteen seventy-eight, welders secretly patched a brand new New York skyscraper, every single night.
Before we go deep into today's story, take a second to like this video and subscribe if you haven't. Let's get into it.
It stood fifty-nine stories high on giant stilts, and it had just opened.
The building rules only asked about wind hitting the flat sides.
But a student asked about corner winds, and the numbers showed about forty percent more force.
Then the engineer learned the builders had swapped his welded joints for bolts to save money.
A big enough storm could snap those bolts, right in the middle of Manhattan.
You see, a weld turns a joint into one solid piece. Bolts are only as strong as the bolts.
Every night after the offices emptied, welders covered the bolted joints with steel plates.
During the repair, Hurricane Ella headed for New York, and evacuation plans were drawn up.
So everyone watched the forecasts, until the storm turned away.
The repair worked, and the public didn't hear about it until nineteen ninety-five.
